cards.claim: Noise scale in SGD dynamics decays proportionally to η/B (learning rate divided by batch size)
cards.conditions: SGD with any batch size and learning rate; follows from stochastic differential equation analysis
cards.effect: The noise scale σ controls magnitude of random fluctuations; it scales as η/B
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis from Smith & Le (2017) extended to show that decay of learning rate simultaneously decays noise scale
cards.quote: the scale of random fluctuations in the SGD dynamics, σ, where σ ∝ η/B, where η is the learning rate, N is the training set size and B is the batch size

cards.claim: Decaying learning rate is equivalent to increasing batch size for maintaining noise scale when η/B is held constant
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum, Nesterov momentum, or Adam; same number of training epochs; tested on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet
cards.effect: Three schedules (decaying LR, hybrid, increasing batch) produce nearly identical training and test curves
cards.evidence: Empirical experiments on wide ResNet (CIFAR-10) and ImageNet with multiple optimizers
cards.quote: we show one can usually obtain the same learning curve on both training and test sets by instead increasing the batch size during training. This procedure is successful for stochastic gradient descent (SGD), SGD with momentum, Nesterov momentum, and Adam. It reaches equivalent test accuracies after the same number of training epochs, but with fewer parameter updates

cards.claim: Momentum coefficient introduces an accumulation timescale of ~(1/(1-β)) epochs where β is momentum, during which parameter updates are suppressed
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum; at initialization when accumulation starts at zero
cards.effect: Accumulation grows exponentially toward steady state over ~(1/(1-β)) epochs; reduces convergence rate during this phase
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis of momentum update equations with empirical observation of training dynamics
cards.quote: the accumulation grows in exponentially towards its steady state value over a 'timescale' of approximately 1/(1-β) training epochs. During this time, the magnitude of the parameter updates is suppressed, reducing the rate of convergence

cards.claim: Increasing momentum coefficient β increases the timescale over which accumulation forgets old gradients, proportional to 1/(1-β) epochs
cards.conditions: SGD with high momentum; when changes in loss landscape occur
cards.effect: When this timescale becomes several epochs long, accumulation cannot adapt to landscape changes, impeding training
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis of momentum dynamics and empirical observation that high momentum causes training impediments
cards.quote: when we increase the momentum coefficient we increase the timescale required for the accumulation to forget old gradients (this timescale is also 1/(1-β)). Once this timescale becomes several epochs long, the accumulation cannot adapt to changes in the loss landscape, impeding training

cards.claim: Scaling learning rate and batch size jointly (when η→αη and B→αB) maintains training dynamics but can be combined with momentum scaling
cards.conditions: When replacing learning rate decay with batch size increases; holds when scaling rules have η/B constant
cards.effect: Can increase initial learning rate and batch size simultaneously without changing convergence to same epoch count
cards.evidence: Experimental validation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet with scaling rule η/B = constant
cards.quote: we can further reduce the number of parameter updates by increasing the learning rate and scaling the batch size. ... Finally, one can increase the momentum coefficient and scale B, although this tends to slightly reduce the test accuracy

cards.claim: Increasing momentum coefficient while scaling batch size reduces test accuracy, despite reducing parameter updates
cards.conditions: Large batch training on CIFAR-10 with momentum 0.98 vs 0.9; same decay schedule for noise scale
cards.effect: Momentum 0.9 achieves 94.4% accuracy (6500 updates); Momentum 0.98 achieves 93.3% accuracy (2500 updates); median across 5 runs shows similar drop
cards.evidence: Direct empirical comparison of test accuracy across scheduling variants
cards.quote: 'Increased momentum coefficient' combines increasing batch sizes during training and the increased initial learning rate of 0.5, with an increased momentum coefficient of 0.98, and an initial batch size of 3200... 'Increased momentum coefficient' requires less than 2500 parameter updates, but reaches a lower test accuracy of 93.3%

cards.claim: When batch size reaches limit where noise scale becomes too small (η/B → 0), learning rate must decay to maintain training effectiveness
cards.conditions: Large batch training; after initial batch size increase phase
cards.effect: Cannot maintain constant learning rate indefinitely; must eventually decay LR
cards.evidence: Theoretical constraint from noise scale analysis; practical limitation in all experiments
cards.quote: The main contribution of this work is to show that it is possible to make efficient use of vast training batches, if one increases the batch size during training at constant learning rate until η/B ≈ 1/N. After this point, we revert to the use of decaying learning rates

cards.claim: Warm-up phase can mitigate instabilities from high initial momentum when using large batch sizes
cards.conditions: Large batch training at initialization; bias correction (as in Adam) can cause instabilities at large B
cards.effect: Reduced learning rate during initial epochs recommended to avoid instability
cards.evidence: Empirical observation and discussion of initialization dynamics
cards.quote: when the batch size is large, we found that this often causes instabilities during the early stages of training. We note that Goyal et al. (2017) recommended a reduced learning rate for the first few epochs
